chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If he is in snow, then let him look to the felt of his saddle and perform tayammum from its dust, or from something from it. And if he is in a state where he finds nothing but clay, then there is no harm in performing tayammum from it.

key_terms.الثَّلْجِ: snow as the surrounding condition in which ordinary earth is inaccessible
key_terms.الطِّينَ: clay or mud, allowed here as a substitute material for tayammum
key_terms.سَرْجِهِ: his saddle, whose felt may contain usable dust
key_terms.غُبَارِهِ: its dust, used as the material for tayammum
key_terms.لِبْدَ: the felt or thick fabric associated with the saddle
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمَ: to perform tayammum, the dry ablution

ai.seo_question: What can a person use for tayammum when surrounded by snow or when only clay is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on tayammum when ordinary earth is unavailable. It permits tayammum using dust found on the felt of a saddle, and if nothing is available except clay, it also permits tayammum with that.
